summary: MGPI's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-22) presents a profitable beverage-alcohol issuer with a 16-year KPMG tenure, no going-concern language, $107M FY23 net income, and adequate liquidity ($337M revolver availability) - none of the AAP/SRPT-style accounting-fraud signals. The thesis is governance/operational, not forensic-accounting: (1) the Atchison Distillery closure (announced July 2023, ceased Dec 2023) eliminates ~$133M / 16% of FY23 revenue going forward, with the 10-K framing it as offensive margin improvement rather than pro-forma reconciling the revenue cliff - visible in Q1 FY24 Distilling Solutions -25% and white-goods/co-products -72% YoY; (2) the Lux family (controlling shareholders from the April 2021 Luxco merger) sold ~$30M of MGPI common stock May 2023-Feb 2024, concentrated in May-Sep 2023 ($28.7M cumulative by Sep) ahead of the Q1 FY24 collapse, with Donn Lux (10%+ owner, board director) filing five May 2023 sales 370 days late on 2024-05-14 (the day before the framework cutoff); (3) on Oct 31, 2023 - the same day the CEO transition agreements (Bratcher in, Colo out) were signed - the board approved a $9M related-party purchase from Director Donn Lux's Kemper-Themis entity, closing Feb 2024 at the same moment cash had fallen from $47.9M to $18.4M; (4) the new CEO David Bratcher is the former president of Luxco, formalizing strategic-control transfer to the Luxco/Branded-Spirits faction within 30 months of the merger; (5) the FY23 10-K outlook (signed 2024-02-22 with ~7 weeks of Q1 FY24 actuals in hand) does not reference Q1 trading - 70 days later the Q1 10-Q discloses consolidated revenue -15%, op income -30%, EPS -34%; (6) customer concentration top-10 jumped +600 bps YoY (36%->44%) with a new >10% individual customer in FY23 (none in FY22/21), unnamed but likely Penelope's distributor; (7) Penelope contingent-consideration revalued up 18% in 9 months ($62M->$73M) - the rare positive datapoint, but goodwill+intangibles are 92% of the $167M purchase price, leaving $95M of unimpaired goodwill if Penelope ever rolls over; (8) Q1 FY24 saw a $7M share buyback initiation at the same moment Lux-family insiders are selling - classic 'insiders sell into the buyback' pattern. Verdict: SHORT-tier on governance/insider/operating-trajectory grounds. Disclosures are mostly honest at the line-item level but materially under-frame the run-rate collapse, the Lux-family liquidity migration, and the control-transfer story.
